resources.string: No profiles yet.\nTap + to create your first profile.

NEXORA stores browser metadata locally per profile. Website cookies and storage use AndroidX WebKit named profiles where supported. Bulk profile creation includes a four-step mobile wizard, per-profile User-Agent and proxy assignments, User-Agent and proxy imports, profile groups, startup tabs, fingerprint preferences and advanced settings. Imported proxy credentials are encrypted using Android Keystore. Current WebView browsing supports only unauthenticated HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy overrides, which remain app-wide. Unsupported proxy and fingerprint modes are not applied. Fingerprint changes remain JavaScript-level, not native Chromium modifications.

NEXORA — Private browsing. Total control.

Version 0.4.0-alpha1 (Bulk Profile Creation)

What is included
- Profile workspace, profile editor and device presets.
- Four-step mobile bulk profile wizard for 1–50 profiles.
- Global defaults, per-profile User-Agent/proxy overrides, group names, remarks and startup tabs.
- User-Agent import with OS/browser detection and duplicate checks.
- Proxy import for SOCKS5, SOCKS4, HTTP and HTTPS with encrypted local credential storage.
- Fingerprint preferences, Do Not Track signal, hardware acceleration and image blocking.
- Existing tabs, tab groups, saved sessions, bookmarks, history, downloads, advanced find, text zoom and redirects.

Engine and limitations
- Built on Android System WebView, a Chromium-based engine supplied by the device. It is not a separately bundled Chromium build.
- Named WebView profiles are required for isolated website storage. If MULTI_PROFILE is unavailable, bulk creation and browser launch are blocked.
- Proxy override is app-wide in this WebView architecture. Only unauthenticated HTTP and SOCKS5 are assignable; authenticated proxies, SOCKS4 and HTTPS are imported for reference but cannot be used for browsing in this release.
- Windows, macOS and Linux browser emulation are not available. iOS presets are emulation only.
- Canvas, WebGL, audio and WebRTC controls remain JavaScript-level. Media-device, client-rect and speech-synthesis controls are not active. IP-based timezone/language and WebRTC Proxy IP modes are unavailable.
- DNT is a browser preference signal, not a guarantee that sites honor it.
- This alpha has passed static checks and parser smoke tests only. Android compilation, installation and physical-device behavior still require verification.

Your IP address is changed by your proxy, not by the browser itself.
